extracted.intended_audience: general readers of literary autobiography / readers of Mark Twain in the North American Review
extracted.subtask_description: A magazine-published chapter of Mark Twain's autobiographical recollections, composed as narrated reminiscences and family-biography vignettes. The text is literary prose intended for general readers and magazine subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frankness/evenhanded biographical honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a frank historian. She doesn't cover up one's deficiencies, but gives them an equal showing with one's handsomer qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Susy's biography aims for candidness—presenting both faults and virtues with equal attention. As an evaluative standard for biography, favor transparency and evenhanded treatment rather than flattering omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal the author's sympathetic nature
rubrics_metrics.description: I have wanted papa to write a book that would reveal something of his kind sympathetic nature, and 'The Prince and the Pauper' partly does it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful work (here, a book) should show the author's humane, sympathetic qualities—not merely jokes or surface humor—but scenes that reveal moral sympathy and tenderness (example: the pauper/mother recognition scene).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality (style should be excellent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book is full of lovely charming ideas, and oh the language! It is _perfect_.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style and diction are central to literary success. Praiseworthy works exhibit felicitous, 'perfect' language in passages (the narrator points to specific scenes described 'so wonderfully'). Emphasize careful, expressive wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety of feeling; blend touching scenes with humor
rubrics_metrics.description: I never saw a man with so much variety of feeling as papa has; now the 'Prince and the Pauper' is full of touching places; but there is most always a streak of humor in them somewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective literary works often combine a range of emotions—deeply touching moments alongside recurring elements of humor. Aim for emotional variety and the ability to shift tone while retaining cohesion (e.g., touching recognition scenes that also contain humorous asides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial restraint / modify or expurgate overly strong passages
rubrics_metrics.description: The passages which were so satisfactory to them always had an element of strength in them which sorely needed modification or expurgation, and were always sure to get it at their mother's hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editing should consider audience sensitivity: passages that seem especially strong or objectionable may require modification or removal. The text illustrates a family-editing practice where mother and children actively excise material deemed too strong—suggesting prudence and audience-aware pruning as part of producing publishable prose.
